title: Canonical tame ramification sequence of a strictly henselian valuation trait
statement: Let $R$ be a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with fraction field $K$ and residue field $k$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Let $K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ be a separable closure [def-pd-separable-closure] inside an algebraically closed field $\Omega$, and let $H=\operatorname{Gal}(K^{\mathrm{sep}}/K)$ with its profinite Krull topology. Put $p=1$ if $\operatorname{char}k=0$, and $p=\operatorname{char}k$ otherwise. For $(d,p)=1$, put $\mu_d(\Omega)=\{z\in\Omega^\times:z^d=1\}$, and let $G=\varprojlim_{(d,p)=1}\mu_d(\Omega)$, with transition $z\mapsto z^{e/d}$ for $d\mid e$ and inverse-limit topology. For a uniformizer $\pi$ choose compatible roots $\pi^{1/d}$. The maps $h\mapsto h(\pi^{1/d})/\pi^{1/d}$ define a continuous surjection $t:H\to G$ independent of these choices and of the uniformizer. Its kernel $S$ is a pro-$p$ group: each finite continuous quotient has $p$-power order; if $p=1$ then $S=1$. Thus $1\to S\to H\xrightarrow{t}G\to1$ is exact. The group $G$ is procyclic: compatible primitive roots give a topological generator $\sigma$, and for each $(d,p)=1$ the subgroup generated topologically by $\sigma^d$ has index $d$.

source.place: Expose XVII, section 1.2 opening paragraph (printed p. 259), tame sequence; see also Stacks Tag 0BUB, pione.tex, lemma-structure-decomposition-separable-closure

proof.text: Write $D=\{d\in\mathbf Z_{>0}:(d,p)=1\}$. Every $d\in D$ is a unit in $R$. For $u\in R^\times$, the separable polynomial $X^d-\bar u$ has a root in the separably closed field $k$, and its derivative there is nonzero. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-root-lifting] to obtain $b\in R^\times$ with $b^d=u$. Also [lem-sbc-strict-local-roots-of-unity] gives exactly $d$ roots of $X^d-1$ in $R$, forming a cyclic group, with distinct residues. These are all its roots in $\Omega$, by the degree bound for a polynomial over a field. Thus $\mu_d(\Omega)\subset R^\times\subset K^\times$, and reduction identifies it with $\mu_d(k)$. Here and below the finite root groups have their discrete topology.

source.place: Tag 04GG, lemma-characterize-henselian, simple-root lifting; Tag 06RR, lemma-uniqueness; compare more-algebra.tex Tag 09EV

proof.text: For each $d\in D$ the roots of $X^d-\pi$ form a nonempty finite set $A_d$ in $K^{\mathrm{sep}}$: the polynomial is separable, since $d$ is nonzero in $K$, and splits in the separable closure. If $d\mid e$, taking the $(e/d)$th power maps $A_e$ onto $A_d$, since an $(e/d)$th root of any $\alpha_d$ is a root of $X^e-\pi$. These maps obey the identity and composition laws. The divisibility poset $D$ is nonempty and directed by least common multiples. Apply [lem-galois-inverse-limit-surjective] to choose a compatible family $\alpha_d=\pi^{1/d}$. Put $K_d=K(\alpha_d)$. The ring $R[T]/(T^d-\pi)$ is a domain by [lem-sbc-dvr-uniformizer-root-algebra]; localizing it at $R\setminus\{0\}$ gives the domain $K[T]/(T^d-\pi)$, so this polynomial is irreducible over $K$. Its roots are $\zeta\alpha_d$ with $\zeta\in\mu_d(K)$ by Step 1. Apply [lem-exc-kummer-binomial-splitting-field]: $K_d/K$ is cyclic Galois of degree $d$, and its character $h\mapsto h(\alpha_d)/\alpha_d$ bijects its Galois group with $\mu_d(K)$. Indeed this character is injective since $\alpha_d$ generates, and both groups have $d$ elements.

source.place: Tag 0BUB, lemma-structure-decomposition-separable-closure, final splitting-field paragraph; fields.tex Tag 09I6, section-Kummer; categories.tex Tag 086J

proof.text: For every finite Galois $L/K$ in $K^{\mathrm{sep}}$, let $B_L$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $L$. A DVR is a PID by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], hence is Noetherian and normal by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-normal-separable-integral-closure-finite] makes $B_L$ finite over $R$. It is a nonzero domain with fraction field $L$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal]. The product decomposition of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-henselian-local-product] has exactly one nonzero factor: two factors would give a nontrivial idempotent in a domain. Consequently $B_L$ is local, with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak n_L$ over that of $R$. By [lem-exc-dvr-galois-degree-data], $B_L$ is a DVR, its residue field $k_L$ is finite over $k$, and $[L:K]=e_L[k_L:k]$, where $e_L=v_L(\pi)>0$ and $v_L$ gives a uniformizer value $1$. Every $K$-automorphism preserves $B_L$ by its monic equations and preserves its unique maximal ideal.

source.place: Tag 09E8, remark-finite-separable-extension; algebra.tex Tags 032L and 04GH, lemma-finite-over-henselian

proof.text: If $p>1$, [lem-pc-kbar-pure-insep] implies that $k_L/k$ is purely inseparable: embed this finite algebraic extension in an algebraic closure of $k$ and restrict the stated purely inseparable extension. Each $x\in k_L$ therefore has $x^{p^a}\in k$ for some $a$, and any $k$-automorphism fixes $x$ because $X^{p^a}-x^{p^a}$ has at most one root in a field of characteristic $p$. If $p=1$, every irreducible polynomial over $k$ is separable (its derivative is nonzero and coprime to it in characteristic zero); separable closedness gives $k_L=k$. In either case every $K$-automorphism of $L$ acts trivially on $k_L$. Thus its decomposition and inertia groups are both $\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)$.

source.place: Tag 030K, lemma-separable-first; the purely inseparable conclusion over a separably closed field; characteristic-zero derivative argument written here

proof.text: Apply Step 3 to $L=K_d$. In $B_{K_d}$ one has $d\,v(\alpha_d)=v(\pi)=e_{K_d}$, so $d\mid e_{K_d}$. But Step 3 and $[K_d:K]=d$ imply $e_{K_d}\le d$. Hence $e_{K_d}=d$ and $\alpha_d$ is a uniformizer. Also $[k_{K_d}:k]=1$. This uses no excellence, perfection, or completeness assumption.

source.place: Tag 0BUB, final paragraph: divisibility of the root-extension ramification index; more-algebra.tex Tag 09E8 gives the degree bound

proof.text: For $h\in H$, put $t_d(h)=h(\alpha_d)/\alpha_d$. Its $d$th power is $1$, so it lies in $\mu_d(K)$ by Step 1. Since $H$ fixes this root group, $t_d(hh')=t_d(h)t_d(h')$. Compatibility of the $\alpha_d$ gives $t_d=t_e^{e/d}$ for $d\mid e$, hence a homomorphism $t:H\to G$. It is continuous: $t_d$ depends only on restriction to the finite Galois field $K_d$, and these restrictions are continuous for the Krull topology. The latter topology is the inverse-limit topology on finite Galois restrictions by [lem-exc-galois-krull-finite-limit]. Continuity of all coordinates is continuity into the subspace inverse limit.

source.place: Tags 0BUA and 0BUB, canonical tame character; fields.tex Tag 0BU2, lemma-infinite-galois-limit

proof.text: Changing $\alpha_d$ for fixed $\pi$ multiplies it by an element of $\mu_d(K)$, fixed by $H$, so $t_d$ is unchanged. For a second uniformizer $\pi'=u\pi$, Step 1 supplies $b_d\in R^\times$ with $b_d^d=u$. Any chosen root $\alpha'_d$ of $\pi'$ equals $b_d\alpha_d\zeta_d$ for $\zeta_d\in\mu_d(K)$, so $h(\alpha'_d)/\alpha'_d=h(\alpha_d)/\alpha_d$. This calculation works at each $d$ and does not require the $b_d$ to have been chosen compatibly. Thus the map to the intrinsic root limit, rather than to a chosen untwisted integer group, is independent of the uniformizer and all root choices.

source.place: Tag 0BUB, canonical character; algebra.tex Tag 04GG, applied in Step 1 to roots of a unit

proof.text: Let $(z_d)_d\in G$. Step 2 gives a unique $K$-automorphism $a_d$ of $K_d$ with $a_d(\alpha_d)=z_d\alpha_d$. If $d\mid e$, its restriction is $a_d$, because $(z_e\alpha_e)^{e/d}=z_d\alpha_d$. Thus these automorphisms glue to a $K$-automorphism $a$ of $K_t=\bigcup_d K_d$; the compatible inverse automorphisms give its inverse. The field $K_t/K$ is normal: each of its elements lies in a finite normal $K_d$, so its minimal polynomial splits there. The separable closure $K^{\mathrm{sep}}/K$ is also normal: the conjugates of a separable algebraic element are again separable algebraic and belong to this closure. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normal-subextension-automorphism-extends] to extend $a$ to $h\in H$. Then $t(h)=(z_d)_d$. This proves surjectivity in both residue characteristics.

source.place: Tag 0BME, lemma-lift-maps (2), normal extension of embeddings, as packaged in the cited normal-subextension automorphism lemma; pione.tex Tag 0BUB, root-field realization

proof.text: Assume now $p>1$. For each finite Galois $L/K$, Step 4 identifies its inertia group with $H_L=\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)$. Apply [lem-exc-finite-dvr-tame-inertia]: with a uniformizer $w_L$ of $B_L$, $\chi_L(h)=\overline{h(w_L)/w_L}$ is a surjective character to $\mu_{n_L}(k_L)$, whose kernel $P_L$ is a finite $p$-group, where $e_L=q_Ln_L$, $q_L$ is a $p$-power and $(n_L,p)=1$. Step 1 identifies $\mu_{n_L}(k_L)$ with $\mu_{n_L}(k)$: it already supplies $n_L$ distinct roots in $k$, which exhaust the roots in $k_L$. Define $\theta_L=\chi_L^{q_L}$, which has the same kernel and is surjective since raising to $q_L$ is an automorphism of a cyclic group of order $n_L$.

source.place: Tag 09EE, lemma-galois-inertia and equation-inertia-character; Tag 0BU8, remark-canonical-inertia-character

proof.text: For $M\supseteq L$ finite Galois, the maximal ideal of $B_M$ contracts to that of $B_L$: its residue field is a finite-dimensional domain over $k$, and so is a field; uniqueness in Step 3 applies. Thus [lem-exc-finite-tame-character-tower] applies to these very primes. It gives surjective restrictions $H_M\to H_L$ and $P_M\to P_L$, $n_L\mid n_M$, and $\theta_L(h|_L)=\theta_M(h)^{n_M/n_L}$. The root-group transition maps obey the identity and composition laws because their exponents multiply; the group and kernel transitions are restriction. The indexing set of finite Galois subfields is nonempty and directed, and $H\cong\varprojlim H_L$ topologically, by [lem-exc-galois-krull-finite-limit]. Apply [lem-exc-infinite-tame-inverse-limit]. We obtain a continuous surjection $\theta:H\to C=\varprojlim_L\mu_{n_L}(k)$ with kernel $P=\varprojlim P_L$, and every finite continuous quotient of $P$ has $p$-power order.

source.place: Tag 0BUA, lemma-structure-decomposition, inverse-limit paragraph; more-algebra.tex Tags 0BU7 and 0BU8

proof.text: Every $d\in D$ occurs as $n_{K_d}=d$ by Step 5. Identify $G$ with the root limit over $k$ by Step 1. A compatible family $(z_d)_d$ maps to $(z_{n_L})_L\in C$. Conversely, from $(c_L)_L\in C$, define $z_d=c_L^{n_L/d}$ using any $L$ with $d\mid n_L$, for instance $K_d$. Two choices have a common finite Galois overfield $M$, and their displayed expressions both equal $c_M^{n_M/d}$. The same calculation proves $z_e^{e/d}=z_d$. These maps are inverse: to recover $c_L$, use that very $L$ at order $n_L$. Each coordinate of either map depends on one input coordinate through a power map between finite groups, so both maps are continuous. This explicitly gives the topological isomorphism $G\cong C$.

source.place: Tag 0BUB, cofinality of the tame indices; two-sided coordinate calculation, not a hidden appeal to cofinality of the fields K_d among all finite extensions

proof.text: At $L=K_d$, Step 5 makes $\alpha_d$ a uniformizer and $q_{K_d}=1$. Hence $\theta_{K_d}(h)=\overline{h(\alpha_d)/\alpha_d}=\overline{t_d(h)}$. Under the reduction identification of Step 1, the isomorphism in Step 11 therefore carries $t$ exactly to $\theta$, coordinate by coordinate at every $d$. Consequently $S=\ker t=P$, topologically, and Step 10 proves the required finite-quotient assertion for $S$ when $p>1$.

source.place: Tag 0BUB, identification of the canonical tame character on root extensions; more-algebra.tex Tag 0BU8

proof.text: Now suppose $p=1$. For each $L$ of Step 3, Step 4 gives $k_L=k$, and every automorphism acts trivially on it. For a uniformizer $w_L$, put $\chi_L(h)=\overline{h(w_L)/w_L}$. Writing $\pi=u_L w_L^{e_L}$ and applying $h$ gives $\chi_L(h)^{e_L}=1$, because $\overline{h(u_L)/u_L}=1$. The equality $h(h'(w_L))/w_L=h(h'(w_L)/w_L)h(w_L)/w_L$ proves multiplicativity after reduction. If $\chi_L(h)=1$, the automorphism of the DVR $B_L$ is finite-order, fixes its residue field, and satisfies $h(w_L)/w_L\equiv1$ modulo its maximal ideal. By [lem-per-dvr-char-zero-tangent-kernel] it is the identity on $B_L$, hence on its fraction field $L$. Thus $\chi_L$ is injective. Only the characteristic-zero finite-order congruence lemma is newly required here.

source.place: Tag 09EE, lemma-galois-inertia, equation-inertia-character and proof of (3), characteristic-zero case

proof.text: For $M\supseteq L$ finite Galois in this characteristic-zero case, write $w_L=v w_M^r$ in the DVR $B_M$, with $v$ a unit. Valuations of $\pi$ give $e_M=r e_L$. Reducing $h(w_L)/w_L=(h(v)/v)(h(w_M)/w_M)^r$ gives $\chi_L(h|_L)=\chi_M(h)^{e_M/e_L}$, since $h$ fixes the residue field. Let $h\in S$ and fix $L$. Take a finite Galois $M$ containing both $L$ and $K_{e_L}$. Since $e_{K_{e_L}}=e_L$ by Step 5, this formula applied to both subfields gives $\chi_L(h|_L)=\chi_{K_{e_L}}(h|_{K_{e_L}})$. The right side is $1$, as $h\in S$ fixes every $\alpha_d$, and hence fixes $K_{e_L}$. Step 13 gives $h|_L=1$. The union of finite Galois subfields is $K^{\mathrm{sep}}$, as in [lem-exc-galois-krull-finite-limit], so $h=1$. Thus $S=1$ when $p=1$. Together with Step 8 and the definition $S=\ker t$, this establishes the asserted exact sequence in every case.

source.place: Tag 09EE, characteristic-zero kernel; the raw uniformizer-character tower formula is computed here; pione.tex Tag 0BUB

proof.text: It remains to produce compatible primitive roots in $\Omega$. By [lem-sc-primitive-root], the set $E_d$ of primitive $d$th roots is finite and nonempty. If $d\mid e$, the power map $E_e\to E_d$ is onto. Indeed choose primitive $\eta_e$; the prescribed target is $(\eta_e^{e/d})^a$ for an integer $a$ prime to $d$. Choose $b\equiv a\pmod d$ and $b\equiv1\pmod r$ for each prime $r\mid e$ not dividing $d$, using [lem-pc-crt-ideal-quotient-product] over $\mathbf Z$. These ideals are pairwise coprime, and the resulting $b$ is prime to $e$, so $\eta_e^b$ is the required primitive lift. The transition maps satisfy identity and composition. Apply [lem-galois-inverse-limit-surjective] to this inverse system of primitive-root sets to obtain $(\zeta_d)_d\in G$ with every $\zeta_d$ primitive. Write $\sigma=(\zeta_d)_d$.

source.place: Tag 09HW, section-roots-of-1; algebra.tex Tag 00DT, lemma-chinese-remainder; categories.tex Tag 086J, lemma-nonempty-limit

proof.text: A basic open subset of $G$ specifies finitely many coordinates; choose $e\in D$ divisible by their indices. Since $\zeta_e$ generates $\mu_e(\Omega)$, some integer power of $\sigma$ matches any given point at coordinate $e$, hence at all those coordinates. Thus $\langle\sigma\rangle$ is dense. Fix $d\in D$. The coordinate projection $G\to\mu_d(\Omega)$ is onto because it contains all powers of $\zeta_d$, and its kernel $U_d$ is closed. Every power of $\sigma^d$ lies in $U_d$. Conversely, for $x\in U_d$ and any finite-coordinate neighborhood, choose $e$ divisible by $d$ and those indices, and write $x_e=\zeta_e^a$. Then $1=x_d=\zeta_d^a$ implies $d\mid a$, so $\sigma^a\in\langle\sigma^d\rangle$ lies in the neighborhood. Hence $\overline{\langle\sigma^d\rangle}=U_d$. Its cosets are the $d$ fibers of that surjective coordinate projection, giving index exactly $d$, including $d=1$.

The proof follows Stacks 0BUA/0BUB and 09EE. For p>1, every hypothesis of the tower and inverse-limit nodes is checked, and the G≅C comparison is identified through K_d. For p=1, S=1 via the new node and the χ_L restriction formula.
